cohort: 1720 pregnant women aged 18-45 years at a gestational age of less than 17 weeks attending health facilities in the Niger Delta, Nigeria
finding: Pregnant women exposed to high levels of oil pollution had a significantly increased risk of premature rupture of membranes and postpartum hemorrhage, indicating the need for interventions to reduce maternal exposure to oil pollution.
mod_finding: While women in high exposure areas had a higher incidence of caesarean section compared to those in low exposure areas, this association was not statistically significant after adjusting for confounding factors.
